items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: So I called Clarence Robinson at the Apollo... And he says... Well Clarence went down the street... and found Lena sitting in there

ctx.x: Well, Lena came to us under a distressed circumstances on our part, and strangely enough through the Apollo. We were playing a two day theater up in the Bronx

called the Casino Theater, and I had a -- I had Ford Leary and Bob Carroll and I had a girl singer, too. I can't remember what her name was. Anyway, they all came down with laryngitis. Not one of them could make a sound. And this was one of these theaters where the band was the whole show. We had to play, put on, you know, an hour, hour and ten minute show, and if you've got no vocalists there again we get back to what I was talking about earlier, the static idea of watching a band play without something else…

stage, and she went on, and this was -- believe it or not this was an Irish neighborhood in the Bronx, and they are inclined to be very chintzy about -- like the manager came back and he said, "I don't know what's going to happen here." I said, "Never mind." And she went on and broke it up. And then of course I asked her to stay and she did, and she was with us for, oh, I think about nine months after that.
